chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, who raised it to Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: concerning
Regarding wiping the feet and wiping the head, he said: "The wiping of the head is once, from the front of the head and its back; and the wiping of the feet is their outer side and their inner side."

His statement, "and the wiping of the feet is their outer side and their inner side," means forward and backward: from the toes to the ankles, and from the ankles to the toes, according to what we have previously presented, and this further clarifies it.

key_terms.مَسْحُ الرَّأْسِ: wiping the head as part of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.مَسْحِ الْقَدَمَيْنِ: wiping the two feet in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.مُقَدَّمِ الرَّأْسِ: the front part of the head

ai.seo_question: How should the head and feet be wiped in wudu (ablution) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the manner of masḥ in wudu (ablution), stating that the head is wiped once and that the feet are wiped on both aspects described as outer and inner. The concluding clarification explains this as wiping in both directions, from the toes to the ankles and from the ankles to the toes, emphasizing the legal details of ritual purity.
